title: Rate limiting
objective: Limit how fast a client can call a service, and see why a token bucket handles bursts better than a fixed window.

sources.title: Claude Platform docs: Rate limits (an example of a real API's limits; over-limit requests get HTTP 429)
IETF RFC 6585: HTTP status code 429 Too Many Requests

simplifies: One client and one limiter in memory. Real limiters are shared across many servers (often in a store like Redis), limit per user or per key, and tell clients when to retry (a Retry-After header). A sliding window is a third common method.

quiz.prompt: Limit 100 a second, fixed window. A client sends 100 at 0.99 s and 100 at 1.01 s. How many get through?

options.explanation: Right. Each burst lands in a different window, so both are allowed: 200 within 0.02 s.
That is the intent, but the window resets at 1.00 s.

quiz.prompt: What should a well-behaved client do when it gets 429 Too Many Requests?

options.text: Wait (as long as Retry-After says, if given) and retry later
options.explanation: Right. Retrying at once just adds to the overload.
That makes the problem worse for everyone.
